newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse consolidation now sensible - traders.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse consolidation now sensible - traders.

text.p: The Brussels bourse ended a bumpy but fairly thinly-traded Friday with light losses as Wall Street moved lower, and traders said they now hoped for a period of consolidation after the steep rise so far this year.

"It would be sensible to consolidate now. There is no big downside risk for the time being but we have overstated the fundamentals on a number of shares and will need good earnings surprises to push the market higher," one trader said.
Traders said the Bel-20 .BFX had fluctuated uncertainly during the day, eventually being hit by the losses in the Dow Jones .DJI and restated U.S. fourth quarter GDP figures.
GDP growth was revised down to 3.9 percent in the fourth quarter from an initial 4.7 percent US-ECI. Analysts had expected a revision down to 4.1 percent.
Fast food retailer Quick was the day's biggest percentage gainer, rising 3.3 percent to 1,900 francs.

Traders said the rise in part reversed price falls that followed news last week of poor 1996 results and a feeling among a number of analysts that Quick might see an improvement in margins from its plans to restore some outlets and open others.

Steelmaker Cockerill Sambre also performed well, rising 1.6 percent to 125 francs. Traders said it was a sympathy reaction after news of a long-awaited joint venture deal between Belgium's Usines Gustave Boel and the Netherlands' Hoogovens.
"Any good news in the sector will always benefit Cockerill," one trader said.
Glassmaker Glaverbel was the star of the show in the morning, rising five percent to 4,200 francs after reporting better-than-expected annual results late on Thursday.
It ended the day up three percent at 4,115 francs.
Group net profit more than doubled in 1996, boosted by extraordinaries, with better operating results seen in 1997.
Group net profit rose to 1.768 billion francs from 621 million in 1995, after extraordinary profit of 606 million.
This included a net capital gain of 1.166 billion francs from the sale of Glaverbel's stake in U.S. glass group AFG Industries.
"The results were not wonderful but they were a lot better than analysts' forecasts," said one trader.
"All in all, the sentiment is friendly after the figures," another trader said.
Retailer Delhaize also had a good day, rising just under one percent to 2,045 francs. Traders said it was mainly due to the strength of the dollar.
The Bel-20 share index ended the day 4.13 points lower at 2,142.42, having moved in a 2,148.15/2,136.21 range.
There were 14 losers, three gainers and three unchanged.
A relatively low -- by recent standards -- total of 2.6 francs worth of Belgian shares changed hands.
